records.title: Here is a GIFT: Enforcing User Data Isolation in LLM Serving via GPU Information Flow Tracking
records.reason: GIFT and GIFT-CC enforce user-data isolation during LLM serving using GPU information-flow tracking and encryption. The primary objective is privacy/security, not inference efficiency. The authors evaluate effects on serving throughput and latency (including up to 4-10.7% throughput overhead in the abstract and optimization-specific overheads), leaving a narrow but direct systems-performance connection; retained as borderline.

records.title: JITterFlip: Uncovering Fault Attack Surfaces in JIT-Compiled LLM Serving
records.reason: JITterFlip studies a Rowhammer fault attack on the JIT serving control plane. It demonstrates corrupt-output and correct-output latency-amplification attacks (up to 124.97x) against inference execution; its objective is to expose and characterize a vulnerability, not to improve inference efficiency or serving performance. The latency result is an attack impact, not an optimization gain.

records.title: Substrate-Portable Execution for Production LLM Workflows
records.reason: The paper exposes inference as a workflow primitive so one agent graph can use streaming, durable asynchronous, or cross-invocation batch inference. It reports no detectable output-quality difference across bindings and describes batch pricing as the primary workflow-level cost lever. However, measured Flink execution has 33–152× end-to-end latency versus streaming, and the primary contribution is workflow portability and access to provider batch pricing rather than reducing inference computation or improving serving efficiency. Relevant to inference deployment economics but indirect under the inference-optimization focus.

records.title: Router Prior Bias: Preserving Base Routing Structure in MoE Post-Training
records.reason: The primary source defines Router Prior Bias as a training-time bias that anchors router logits to a prior from a frozen base router while leaving the router trainable (abstract and §3). The paper compares post-training objectives on Moonlight-16B-A3B and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base; its results are downstream task accuracy and routing retention, not inference latency, memory, or compute savings (§4-5). The evaluation removes the training-time prior hook and probes in inference mode to measure the trained router; inference mode is an evaluation protocol, not an inference-efficiency method.

records.title: A Measurement Study of LLM Inference Trade-offs Across Edge Continuum Hardware
records.reason: This controlled study compares LLM inference, quantization and deployment platform across Jetson Orin, server GPU and server CPU, measuring accuracy, latency, model footprint and energy. records.title: An Open-Source End-to-End FHE Implementation for Privacy-Preserving Llama 3 8B Inference
records.reason: Odin implements end-to-end fully homomorphic Llama-3-8B inference. Although privacy is the deployment premise, the paper directly optimizes the encrypted inference execution path: on one H100 with a 128-token input, it reports full 32-layer ciphertext computation falling from 1651.9 s with THOR to 366.4 s (4.51x); it also reports 58.9 GiB peak memory. Cross-paper FHE latency numbers are explicitly not directly comparable due to different models/protocols/hardware.

records.title: Accelerating Dense LLMs via L0-regularized Mixture-of-Experts
records.reason: The method transforms dense LLM checkpoints into sparsely activated MoEs using L0 regularization, with the explicit goal of accelerating inference. Across Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen2-7B, it reports up to 2-2.5x inference speedup under a common SGLang evaluation setup while retaining comparable quality. Limitations include no 70B evaluation and limited comparison with large MoEs.

records.title: Global Ranks Survive, Selected Heads Shift: BOS-Sink Topology under 4-bit Weight-Only Quantization
records.reason: This empirical study tests whether attention-sink head maps transfer from bf16 to 4-bit quantized models and gives calibration guidance for sink-aware edge deployment. It finds global rank correlations >=0.980 while top-k membership retention is 76.5-88.5%, and the authors explicitly state STC measures topology, not task impact. It is relevant to deploying quantized inference-time attention policies, but does not demonstrate inference latency, throughput or end-task gains; retained as borderline.

records.title: Beyond Scalar Sensitivity: Activation-Aware Mixed-Precision LLM Quantization with Cross-Layer Refinement
records.reason: CASA is a post-training quantization allocation method targeting a fixed low-bit model budget. It uses activation-aware sensitivity and cross-layer refinement; on five LLMs it compares perplexity and six-task accuracy, with gains over the scalar-proxy baseline particularly at 2.25–2.75 bits per weight. Weight quantization under a memory budget enables smaller inference models. Evidence demonstrates model quality under quantization rather than serving latency or tokens/s.
